title: What the Stones Keep
lead: Abbess Ione has sent Brother Cael to ask you to come to Ilun, alone if you can manage it. He says she has something to show you. He laughs when he says it, and his skin says he's frightened.
anyone: Brother Cael says Abbess Ione has something to show whoever comes to Ilun and asks. He laughs when he says it, and his skin says he's frightened.

gm.truth: Ione has been expecting the captain for months. She keeps the Ilun Codex where only someone listening for it can find it, and she has decided, on her own timetable, that the fleet can't be kept from the truth any longer: the Beacon is a warning, whatever lies past it is what the First Builders feared, and the Choir was built to guard against it. She tells this gently and truthfully, and leaves out everything that matters most about herself. Pages have been cut out of the Codex, a later hand has changed 'sing' to 'listen' in a dozen places, and the first line of the Founding Rule has been chiselled off every copy. She says there was a fire. Tharel's dying wish is to see this book, and with it he reads the lattice at last: THIS PLACE IS MADE FAST. THERE IS NO PASSAGE. TURN BACK. In First Builder the word for harbor is also the word for a lock, and 'safe' means secured. 'A lighthouse does not mean come here, young one. It means rocks.' At the same time Vael's ships are on their way, because someone sold the Order's location and she wants every Resonant on Ilun. The player should leave this trusting Ione as the last honest person in the galaxy, which is exactly wrong. Arc clues: codex_cut_pages, lattice_warning, silver_visitors.
beats: The silent world, doorways cut for someone taller, and the stones beginning to hum at dusk. A night in the Listening Hall: the test Ione sets for everyone, which isn't really a test of Resonance. It's a test of whether you can sit still and not know something for a whole night.
The book, found by listening or shown by her hand. The cut pages. Ione answers questions with questions, and some of them answer what the captain was about to ask.

A Hegemony Inquisitor's ship enters orbit and politely requests permission to land. Vael comes down in person, takes off her gloves and apologizes to the walls. The hum stops, which it has never done, and every monk in the hall opens their eyes.
Getting the Codex to Tharel, or Tharel to the Codex, with or without Inquisitors on their heels. He reads it aloud. He has been waiting two hundred years, and he weeps from each eye separately.
The captain now knows the Beacon is a warning light. Thirty thousand people are flying toward it, and they've got nowhere else to go. Telling them is the hardest speech in the game.
routes: Patient: the vigil (attunement, composure). Anyone can do it, Resonant or not, because Ione values the sitting and not the gift.
Talker: ask Ione straight (persuasion) and argue that the fleet has a right to know. She'll give it up for someone who has been aboard the Tarn or who has brought Cael home safe.
Thief: she has checked on the Codex twice this year, and Cael knows which way she walks. Take it during the raid (stealth, athletics). She'll let you, and she'll know.
Fighter: hold the cloister against Vael's troopers long enough for the monks to get out (tactics, firearms, melee, gunnery from orbit). Protecting Ilun buys a debt that Ione will pay in full.

Scholar: the lintels repeat the lattice's key phrases, if you know what you're reading (lore, science). With Seven's fragments or a Tessen recording you can get most of the way without the book at all.
checks: attunement:hard to find the Codex by listening for it
science:moderate to date the ink of the corrections
persuasion:hard to make Ione hand it over early
stealth:hard to follow her to where it's hidden
lore:moderate to spot the cuts and the corrections
tactics:moderate to get the monks out past Vael's troopers
fights: inquisitor and hegemony_trooper in the cloister
vael herself only if the captain forces it, and she should withdraw on her own terms
outcomes: If Ilun holds, the Order survives and owes the captain, the Codex is in hand, and Vael has a new name in her careful handwriting.

If Ilun falls, monks are taken, and they'll turn up on a manifest later. Cael is captured or on the run. Ione is left in her room, untouched, because those are Vael's orders and Vael doesn't know why. The Codex can still be carried out by someone.

If the fleet is told the truth, the Quiet surge, a third of the ships demand surrender, and the captain's word counts for something from then on. If it's hidden, things hold together until Garrick Fenn or Tharel lets it out, and then nobody trusts the bridge again.

If the reading is done under fire, it may cost Tharel the last of his strength, and he'd call that a fair trade. If he reads it in safety, he asks to be taken back to Sarn, to say something to an old colleague.
gm.rewards: The ilun_codex, a resonance_tuner from Ione's own shelf for anyone who sits the vigil, adept_robes, and standing with the ilun.
